model.name: Late blight disease severity values
model.summary: Daily disease severity values (0–4) from hours of high humidity and their temperature, accumulated from potato emergence (or a date you enter, such as tomato transplanting or the last spray) to time fungicide sprays for late blight of potato and tomato.

inputs.name: hours_rh_over_90_from_6pm
inputs.label: Hours with RH ≥ 90%
inputs.description: Day from 6 pm the evening before

biofix.label: Crop emergence or the last fungicide application

model.risk_criteria: Very high: 21 or more DSVs in the last 14 days once the season total reaches 30. High: 14 or more in 14 days once the total reaches 18. Moderate: a season total of 18 or more (the usual first-spray threshold). Low: any DSVs in the last 14 days. Very low: none.
model.guidance_html:
• UW Vegetable Pathology treats a season total of 18 DSVs as the threshold for a first protective fungicide spray. UMass Extension expects disease 7 to 10 days after the total reaches 18 if the pathogen is present.
  • After you spray, enter the spray date to restart the count, so the total shows the weather since your crop was last protected.
  • High and Very high mean recent weather has strongly favored late blight. Keep protection in place and the spray interval short, and scout often.
  • Watch for confirmed late blight reports nearby, in UW Vegetable Pathology's weekly Vegetable Crop Update. A low total doesn't protect a field where late blight is already present. See the late blight topic page for management.
